topic: distributed/cloud systems; consensus; HPC runtime; edge-AIGC performance evaluation
status: bounded research-design lead from one stratified cell; not a prevalence estimate or novelty claim
claim: A performance headline in distributed/cloud research can be supported by fundamentally different evidence: formal asymptotic/probabilistic guarantee (GHAST, asynchronous DKG), tight model-specific lower bound (two-step consensus), single-platform primitive microbenchmark (DART-MPI), simulation (edge ToT provisioning), or an incompletely specified beta-net deployment datapoint without matched comparison (TrueChain). These evidence types answer different questions and should not be compared as though they were the same kind of observed speedup. This seven-paper cell motivates an audit of claim-to-evidence calibration but cannot establish how common overstatement is in the field.
positive_evidence: DART-MPI reports concrete operation-level latency overheads on a Cray XE6; the evidence is measured but platform/primitive-specific.
GHAST proves a confirmation bound under an explicit network/adversary model; the 3d comparison is explicitly a no-observable-attack, equal-confidence case.
A-DKG gives expected-round and communication complexity under f<n/3 and PKI assumptions; it is not a latency benchmark.
The edge-AIGC paper's abstracted percentage gains are simulation results after Qwen creative-writing calibration, not live edge measurements.

TrueChain reports >2,000 TPS in a beta-net live deployment for committee gossip degree below one-sixth committee size, but the inspected paper does not give a matched baseline or detailed workload/latency/reproducibility breakdown; it also notes throughput/security and eclipse-risk tradeoffs.
The two-step consensus paper demonstrates that even a lower-bound mismatch can be caused by differing fast-decision specifications; its two tight bounds differ for task versus object formulations.
counterevidence: The papers are heterogeneous and not a controlled comparison; measured DART-MPI microbenchmarks, TrueChain beta-net throughput, mathematical guarantees, and simulated DSAC results cannot be pooled.
A theorem can be stronger evidence for a model-specific guarantee than an empirical benchmark; evidence classes are complementary, not a single quality ranking.
Only seven records from one frame cell were inspected; no prevalence or abstract-overclaim rate has been estimated.

sources.sections: Cray XE6 setup, low-level benchmark results, reported operation overhead
abstract/system design; committee gossip tradeoff; beta-net >2,000 TPS report at §4.4
abstract confirmation theorem and no-observable-attack comparison
A-DKG resilience, expected rounds, communication bounds
revised fast-consensus definition and tight task/object bounds
Qwen creative-writing experiment, DSAC simulation and reported maxima

falsifiable_test: Preregister a multi-year stratified audit of distributed/cloud/edge papers. Two independent coders, blinded to the study hypothesis, classify each paper's central headline claims, strongest supporting evidence class, model/baseline/workload coverage, and whether abstract wording is bounded accordingly; adjudicate disagreements and separately test abstracts against tables/theorems. The lead is weakened if broad claims are consistently supported by diverse, sufficiently specified workloads and measurements or clearly stated model bounds, and independent replications. Not conducted in this batch.
limitations: Seven randomly sampled records from one topic cell and four arXiv time bands; no external replication search for every paper, no comprehensive deployment evidence search, and no population estimate. TrueChain assessment is limited to the inspected arXiv source; newer implementations or independent evaluations may exist and require a dedicated citation search.

topic: permissionless blockchain consensus; committee communication topology; throughput and security evaluation
status: single-paper quantitative lead with independent conceptual support; not a causal estimate or novelty claim
claim: TrueChain's arXiv v3 reports roughly 80 TPS when BFT committee messages traverse the public PoW gossip network and over 2,000 TPS in a beta-net deployment using a private gossip overlay among a rotating committee. The authors connect the overlay to throughput and explicitly warn that gossip degree trades throughput against committee security, with small/poorly connected overlays vulnerable to eclipse-style risks. GHAST supplies related model-level evidence that optimistic low-confirmation operation and attack-time liveness/security response are distinct operating regimes. The >25× TrueChain ratio is not a controlled causal effect: workloads, network conditions, and other configurations are not shown matched in the paper.
positive_evidence: TrueChain §4.4 describes the ~80 TPS public-gossip case and >2,000 TPS beta-net private committee-gossip case; committee size example is 31, with gsize 4, and authors report throughput/security tradeoffs and potential eclipse risk.

GHAST proves an O(d log(1/epsilon)) confirmation guarantee under a bounded adversarial-power/network-delay model and uses adaptive weights to handle attack conditions; no-attack confirmation results do not describe attack-time performance.
counterevidence: The two TrueChain throughput figures do not come with a matched workload, transaction mix, hardware/network setup, repetitions, or latency distribution in the inspected paper, so dividing them does not identify the causal effect of topology.
TrueChain's beta-net throughput is a paper-reported datapoint; no independent measurement of that exact configuration was located in this limited pass.
GHAST and TrueChain use different designs/models and are not a direct comparison; the GHAST theorem does not validate TrueChain's throughput/security claims.

sources.sections: §4.4 secure communication channel; 80 TPS public gossip; >2,000 TPS beta-net; gsize and eclipse-risk discussion
abstract and confirmation/liveness guarantees under adversarial power and network-delay assumptions

falsifiable_test: Reproduce the same consensus implementation and hold hardware, WAN topology, block/transaction workload, committee size, and adversarial behavior fixed. Randomize public PoW gossip versus private committee-gossip overlays across repeated runs; sweep committee gossip degree. Report sustained TPS, p50/p95/p99 confirmation latency, orphan/reorg rate, safety/liveness events, packet load, and resilience to eclipse/DDoS/adaptive adversaries. The topology-performance-security claim is weakened if private committee gossip does not reproducibly increase throughput, or if gains vanish after matched workload/network controls or incur unacceptable attack/safety costs.
limitations: Primary quantitative signal is one 2018 paper's two reported settings with incomplete measurement detail. GHAST only provides conceptually related formal regime evidence. No protocol implementation, current deployment, or independent replication was tested; not a novel result claim.
